text:
sam: Heads up — customers reporting a spike of ~150-200 502s for the hosted text-generation endpoint in us-west-2 starting ~09:12 UTC. Mostly on streaming calls, they see an immediate 502 mid-stream :frowning: 

jordan: Any trace IDs or example request? Are these from the same route/model?

sam: Same route (hostedapi/v1/stream), same model version pinned. Example curl we used to repro: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":512,"stream":true}' https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Trace header we saw attached: x-request-id=8a7b2f3b (added to logs)

eng-bot: deploy 3401234400 -> edge-proxy-config rolled out to 20% of hosts at 09:04 UTC, rollout paused at 09:10 UTC (manual).

maya: Logs from one ingress host around 09:12: 
```
[09:12:21] envoy [warning] upstream reset while reading response header from upstream, connection: 0x7f8f, reason: connection closed
[09:12:21] nginx [error] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.10.4.23, server: api, request: "POST /v1/stream"
[09:12:22] edge-proxy: conn-reuse fail: downstream keepalive timeout expired, upstream active streams dropped
```

jordan: That looks like an upstream close during active streaming. Could be connection drain timing / keepalive mismatch between frontdoor and runtime. Did the new edge-proxy-config touch keepalive or drain settings?

eng-bot: edge-proxy-config (3401234400) changed downstream_keepalive_timeout from 60s -> 30s and drain_delay from 45s -> 10s.

sam: oh — that explains the timing. Customers with long-lived streams get cut when the host draines and upstream closes faster than frontdoor expects.

maya: Repro steps I used (local): start a long stream from a client, then trigger graceful drain on a single ingress with `kubectl -n edge annotate pod edge-ingress-xyz evict=true` — observed upstream close and client sees 502 at ~30s after drain.

jordan: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback the keepalive/drain change on ingress hosts; 2) increase downstream_keepalive_timeout to previous 60s or 90s; 3) transparent fallback to non-streaming for affected customers (temporary).

liz: Ops request: can we patch config to set downstream_keepalive_timeout=90s and drain_delay=40s for the canary subset and monitor 502 rate? Also create a short-lived synthetic streaming probe to target the canary.

sam: I'll open a customer-facing support note asking impacted customers to switch to short-polling in the meantime (we have a fallback param).

jordan: I'll push a config rollback to the 20% canary with keepalive=90s now, run the synthetic probe (script below).
```
# streaming probe (bash)
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROBE_TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1024,"stream":true}' https://canary.api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/stream &
  sleep 1
done
```

maya: After canary patch: on the three patched hosts p50 latency unchanged, but 502s from streaming dropped from 180->12 in the 10m window. p99 tail still needs observation.

sam: Customer mitigation note posted to the tickets: suggest switching to streaming=false for heavy-tail requests and we'll notify when stable.

liz: Create a follow-up runbook item: requirements for draining while streaming — ensure downstream_keepalive_timeout >= drain_delay + expected stream tail (recommendation 120s). Add to eng-infra playbook.

jordan: Filed ENG-4521 to revert edge-proxy-config defaults and add a test that simulates graceful drains with long-lived streams. Assigning to eng-sre.

sam: Thanks everyone — patch looks good in canary. I'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and coordinate with support. :thumbsup:

maya: For root cause writeup: change in rollout reduced downstream keepalive from 60->30s which caused active streams to be cut during drain; combination of reduced drain_delay amplified the effect.

sam: Marking thread resolved for now — eng-sre follow-up on ENG-4521 and customer tickets open.
